title: I Let the Repair-Cafe Iron Signup Catch the Chair Who Cut the List

parts.text: I signed line four at 10:04 a.m. and chair Wes had already drawn a line through three names including mine. The board said: SIGN IN ORDER. ONE IRON. NO CHAIR CUTS. I was forty-five, volunteer, holding a ticket that listed four. Wes shrugged. "Chairs are the queue." I photographed the board, the strike, and my ticket. Then I asked for the iron log. At 10:11 the coordinator pinged why Wes's name was on a cut list. I kept my voice indoor and let the timestamp talk. I have learned the difference between a title and a line item.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The coordinator can see Wes's strike through my name on the iron signup.

social.video_title: The chair drew a line through my iron slot — Part 1/2
social.description: Repair cafe, a signup board, a chair's strike. I logged the cut. Would you have asked for the iron log?

parts.text: Wes called it triage until the coordinator asked for the still. I printed the log, the board, and the ticket. My name went back. Wes ran the iron in order and told the next chair triage was always about optics. Optics is a word chairs use when a board exists. Signup now has a second line: CHAIRS DO NOT CUT. I keep ticket four. Wes brown-bags his jokes. The table finally looks like a list, not a throne. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.description: Iron log, restored name, and a second line. Was triage ever the board?
